label: monowo
title: ものを
meaning: But...! / But If (you) had just... / But (I) could have... 〜のに！
meaning_example: But if you had just asked, I would have given it to you.

notes.text:
Verb(普通形) + ものを



This grammar is almost always in the form of 〜ば〜ものを。

Sometimes it becomes "もんを" in casual speech.
notes.html:
Verb(普通形) + ものを

This grammar is almost always in the form of 〜ば〜ものを。
Sometimes it becomes "もんを" in casual speech.

notes.text:
〜ものを：　（．．．だったら）〜のに　（実際は〜でなくて残念だという気持ち）

            If only ... had.... , then....would..
notes.html:
〜ものを：　（．．．だったら）〜のに　（実際は〜でなくて残念だという気持ち）
If only ... had.... , then....would..

notes.text:
Expressing the meaning of "although" with the speaker's strong feeling of discontent, regret, blame.

Similar usage to のに 
notes.html:
Expressing the meaning of "although" with the speaker's strong feeling of discontent, regret, blame.
Similar usage to のに 

notes.text: doesn't have to be 「~ば」before 「ものの」but does have to be a conditional clause 「~たら」is ok too.

examples.japanese: 知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもいいものを。
examples.body_text:
知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもいいものを。 

		If you knew, why didn't you tell me!?
examples.body_html:
知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもいいものを。 
If you knew, why didn't you tell me!?

examples.japanese: 人手が足りなかったんですって？ちょっと連絡してくれれば、手伝ってあげたものを。
examples.body_text:
人手が足りなかったんですって？ちょっと連絡してくれれば、手伝ってあげたものを。 

		You didn't have enough people? If you had just called me, I would have helped you.
examples.body_html:
人手が足りなかったんですって？ちょっと連絡してくれれば、手伝ってあげたものを。 
You didn't have enough people? If you had just called me, I would have helped you.

examples.japanese: インターネットで予約すれば簡単にすむものを、彼女は国際電話をかけたんだって。
examples.body_text:
インターネットで予約すれば簡単にすむものを、彼女は国際電話をかけたんだって。 

		If she had just used the internet, she could have easily made the reservation, 
		but 
		she made an international call.
examples.body_html:
インターネットで予約すれば簡単にすむものを、彼女は国際電話をかけたんだって。 
If she had just used the internet, she could have easily made the reservation, but she made an international call.

examples.japanese: 本当のことを言えばいいものを、彼は嘘をついて信用を失ってしまった。
examples.body_text:
本当のことを言えばいいものを、彼は嘘をついて信用を失ってしまった。 

		He should have told the truth, but he lied and lost their trust.
examples.body_html:
本当のことを言えばいいものを、彼は嘘をついて信用を失ってしまった。 
He should have told the truth, but he lied and lost their trust.

examples.japanese: すぐ医者に診（み）てもらったら簡単に治っていた​ものを。手遅れになってしまった。
examples.body_text:
すぐ医者に診（み）てもらったら簡単に治っていた​ものを。手遅れになってしまった。 

If I'd only 
		gone to the doctor right away, I would have gotten better without any trouble. I acted too late.
examples.body_html:
すぐ医者に診（み）てもらったら簡単に治っていた​ものを。手遅れになってしまった。 
If I'd only gone to the doctor right away, I would have gotten better without any trouble. I acted too late.

examples.japanese: 父が後１年生きていたくれたら私の結婚式に出てもらえた​ものを、私がぐずぐずしていたばかりに、父に私の晴れ姿を見てももらえず、とても残念です。
examples.body_text:
父が後１年生きていたくれたら私の結婚式に出てもらえた​ものを、私がぐずぐずしていたばかりに、父に私の晴れ姿を見てももらえず、とても残念です。 

		Had my father live one year longer, he could have attended my wedding ceremony, 
		but just because 
		I was indecisive for so long, I couldn't give him the chance to see me in my wedding dress. I feel so sorry!
examples.body_html:
父が後１年生きていたくれたら私の結婚式に出てもらえた​ものを、私がぐずぐずしていたばかりに、父に私の晴れ姿を見てももらえず、とても残念です。 
Had my father live one year longer, he could have attended my wedding ceremony, but just because I was indecisive for so long, I couldn't give him the chance to see me in my wedding dress. I feel so sorry!

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語を続けて勉強すればいいものを１年間やっただけでやめてしまった。
examples.body_text:
彼は日本語を続けて勉強すればいいものを１年間やっただけでやめてしまった。 

		It would have been better if he'd continued his Japanese studies, 
		but 
		he quite after only one year.
examples.body_html:
彼は日本語を続けて勉強すればいいものを１年間やっただけでやめてしまった。 
It would have been better if he'd continued his Japanese studies, but he quite after only one year.

comments.text:
This can often be replaced with 〜のに

早く言えばよかったのに。

早く言えばよかったものを。



This is used to express the speakers moderate disappointment or regret.
comments.html:

早く言えばよかったものを。

This is used to express the speakers moderate disappointment or regret.

comments.text:
Isn't ものを　always used with 〜た形?

Because, ものを is "but..." where something regrettable happened , and couldn't/almost impossible to be recovered from.

comments.text:
ex# 知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもよかったものを。"If you had known, it would be OK even you told me."(But now it means not OK to the speaker since before this , the listener DIDN'T KNOW about that particular thing and told the speaker about it already.) Sounds strange to me, unless the speaker wanted it to be known to him at that particular time , in that case :

あの時知れば、教えてくれてもよかったものを。





Is better to say :

知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてよかったものを。or

(君が）知っていて教えてくれればよかったものを。"It would be nice if you had known and told me."



I think if you wanted to say : 

" If you have known, why didn't you tell me?" (Of agony) : 知ってるのであれば、どうして教えてくれなかったのよ．．



 "If you have known, isn't it ok to tell me?" : 知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもいいんじゃない（か）。
comments.html:

Sounds strange to me, unless the speaker wanted it to be known to him at that particular time , in that case :
あの時知れば、教えてくれてもよかったものを。


Is better to say :
知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてよかったものを。or
(君が）知っていて教えてくれればよかったものを。"It would be nice if you had known and told me."

I think if you wanted to say :

"If you have known, isn't it ok to tell me?" : 知ってるのであれば、教えてくれてもいいんじゃない（か）。

comments.text: You have to keep in mind that ものを is not a conversational phrase, and it is predominantly literal diction.
